result.title: Draft Calibration for Speculative Decoding: Accelerating LLM Serving by Matching Draft and Target Distributions
result.summary: Speculative decoding accelerates large language model (LLM) inference by employing a lightweight draft model to propose draft tokens and allowing the target model to verify the new tokens in parallel to improve inference-time compute utilization. The speedup relies on the acceptance probability of draft tokens in target verification, which is directly related to the gap $\|p-q\|_1$ between the target distribution $p$ and the draft distribution $q$. In this paper, we study draft calibration of speculative decoding to improve the speedup of speculative decoding, where we employ post-hoc methods to calibrate the draft distribution to mitigate the distribution gap. We observe that though current community open-source draft models may learn the top candidate token correctly, they are generally underconfident compared to the target model, suggesting a consistent distribution mismatch. To mitigate the effect of this mismatch on the acceptance rate of the draft models, we try various post-hoc calibration methods, including standard temperature scaling and token-wise calibration. Our results suggest that a standard temperature scaling applied to the draft distribution improves the acceptance length by up to approximately 10\% with almost no additional cost across different tasks. Throughput analysis further verifies that this improvement in serving efficiency. Analysis of more general calibration methods reveals further potential room for improvement.

AI.brief_summary: 研究 speculative decoding 中 draft 模型相对 target 模型普遍欠自信的分布失配问题，尝试温度缩放与按 token 校准等事后校准方法，发现简单温度缩放可将接受长度提升约 10% 且几乎不增开销。
AI.relevance_reason: 其关于「提案—验证」中接受率与 draft/target 分布差异的分析，可能可供核查 LVR 多步 latent 提案的验证成本、提议器校准与停止决策，但论文本身面向文本服务加速，与视觉状态推理无直接联系。
